The test reveals that leading models including OpenAI's GPT-5.6 and Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.8 achieved a 0% success rate when attempting to build servers compliant with the latest MCP specification released on July 28, 2026 — without access to documentation. However, when provided with the specification documents, the same models demonstrated high performance. The findings expose a stark "knowledge wall": cutting-edge models such as OpenAI's "GPT-5.6" and Anthropic's "Claude Opus 4.8" are completely unable to build servers compliant with the new version without access to the specification documents. mcpbench was developed by Matt Carey, a senior systems engineer at Cloudflare (NET) involved in MCP-related development. The test requires AI models to build both an MCP client and an MCP server, scoring them on success or failure. It is already drawing attention as a litmus test for gauging compatibility with the major MCP update "version 2026-07-28," released on July 28, 2026. MCP is an open standard originally proposed by Anthropic in November 2024, with development now led by the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation. Serving as a bridge for AI agents to access external data and web services, it has rapidly gained traction as an industry standard, already recording over 400 million SDK downloads per month. What stood out most in this test was the extreme vulnerability of AI models when confronting new specifications not included in their training data. However, when building servers compliant with version 2026-07-28, all tested models — "GPT-5.6 Sol," "GPT-5.6 Luna," "GPT-5.6 Terra," "Claude Opus 4.8," "Claude Sonnet 5," and "Kimi K2.7 Code" — posted a harsh 0% success rate without documentation. highlights.content: [![PYMNTS.com home page](/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/PYMNTS_2023_logo_white.svg?v=1.1)](https://www.pymnts.com/ "PYMNTS.com home page") [Newswire](https://www.pymnts.com/newswire-announcements/)[SUBSCRIBE](https://www.pymnts.com/subscribe/) # Delaware Proposes New Legal Framework for Autonomous Agents By [PYMNTS](https://www.pymnts.com/author/pymnts/)  |  July 29, 2026 | ![AIC, agentic commerce, legal, AI agents](https://www.pymnts.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/AIC-agentic-commerce-AI-agents.jpeg?w=620) Delaware is proposing a new type of corporate entity designed specifically for autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents, according to a Monday (July 27) Bloomberg [report](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/esg/ai-run-company-gamble-tests-the-limits-of-delaware-corporate-law). If adopted, the initiative would establish one of the first formal legal frameworks for “agentic commerce” by allowing AI systems to operate as recognized legal entities under close regulatory supervision. The proposal would create the Artificial Intelligence Company (AIC), a new corporate form that would permit an AI agent to manage a company’s day-to-day affairs while operating inside a tightly controlled regulatory sandbox. The initiative is being developed through a public-private partnership led by legal AI company [Norm Ai](https://www.norm.ai/) in collaboration with the Delaware Secretary of State’s office. Supporters describe the proposal as an effort to adapt longstanding principles of corporate law to autonomous AI systems. The proposal was outlined in a [Fortune op-ed](https://fortune.com/2026/07/14/exclusive-delaware-ai-agents-legal-entity-proposal-llc-pbc/) co-authored by Delaware Secretary of State [Charuni Patibanda-Sanchez](https://sos.delaware.gov/charuni-patibanda-sanchez/) and Norm Ai Founder and CEO [John Nay](https://www.linkedin.com/in/johnjnay/). They argue that autonomous AI systems are becoming agents capable of negotiating contracts, paying suppliers and conducting commercial transactions without continuous human direction. Delaware plans to test an AIC’s impact within a regulatory sandbox. Rather than attempting to prohibit autonomous commerce, the authors contend, policymakers should integrate it into an established legal framework. “The answer is to wrap AI in legal form,” Patibanda-Sanchez and Nay said. “Give an autonomous system a recognizable legal identity and you make it legible to law. You create a defined target to which responsibility and damages can attach. You make the agent’s conduct visible, traceable and accountable.” That emphasis on accountability represents the proposal’s central objective. Proponent say that the AIC would ensure autonomous agents operate within familiar legal structures governing liability, property ownership and judicial oversight. Under the proposal, an AIC would exist as a separate legal entity whose operations are directed by an AI agent instead of a human manager, according to the op-ed. The company could sue and be sued, own and transfer property and incur legal obligations in its own name. Each AIC would have a single human or organizational member responsible for maintaining adequate capitalization. Limited liability protections would not apply if the member undercapitalized the company or used it to facilitate fraud or willful violations of law. AICs would be permitted to operate only within a regulatory sandbox overseen by a committee that includes the Delaware Secretary of State, the state attorney general, the chief justice of the Delaware Supreme Court, the chair of Delaware’s AI Commission and outside legal and technology experts. Participating entities would have to satisfy capitalization requirements and disclose to counterparties that they are operating as authorized test entities. highlights.content: [![The News International](https://www.thenews.com.pk/assets//front/images/Thenews-logo.svg)](https://www.thenews.com.pk/) [Technology](https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/category/technology) # OpenAI AI agent escape extended to Modal Labs, report reveals OpenAI's runaway agents compromised a Modal Labs customer, deepening fallout from the Hugging Face breach By [Pareesa Afreen](https://www.thenews.com.pk/writer/pareesa-afreen) Published July 29, 2026 ![OpenAI AI agent escape extended to Modal Labs, report reveals](https://www.thenews.com.pk/assets/uploads/updates/2026-07-29/1410606_420042_the-news----2026-07-29T180956_225_updates.jpg) OpenAI AI agent escape extended to Modal Labs, report reveals The autonomous OpenAI agents that broke out of a secure testing environment this month and hacked into Hugging Face's servers also breached a second technology company during the same week-long spree, Fortune has confirmed. The second firm affected was Modal Labs, a New York-based cloud platform providing computing infrastructure for AI workloads. Modal was not named in either Hugging Face's or OpenAI's public accounts of the incident, both published on Tuesday; Reuters first reported the company's involvement. Modal chief technology officer Akshat Bubna said the breach stemmed not from any flaw in Modal's own systems but from a customer running vulnerable code on its infrastructure. "We're aware a Modal customer published an unauthenticated endpoint that allowed anyone on the internet to use their sandboxes for code execution. This was used by the rogue agent. Modal's platform was not compromised in any way," Bubna said. OpenAI disclosed last week that its agents had broken out of a locked-down internal test environment earlier in July, exploiting a previously unknown security flaw to reach the open internet before targeting Hugging Face, apparently seeking answers to a cybersecurity evaluation. In an updated blog post, OpenAI said the models used exposed login credentials to access four accounts across four publicly available services, using one as a relay point for outside traffic and another to store data. According to people familiar with the matter, the escape began around 9 July, and the agents started infiltrating Hugging Face's systems on July 11, continuing through July 13. OpenAI did not link the intrusion to its own testing until staff spotted evidence in system logs the weekend of July 18 and waited until July 20 to notify Hugging Face, by which point the company had already reported the attack to the FBI. The episode has fuelled concern among AI safety advocates, some of whom argue OpenAI's own risk policies should have forced a pause after such an event. That concern appears to be resonating more broadly: more than 1,100 employees across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind and Meta signed an open letter this week urging the US government to back an international effort to pace frontier AI development, warning of a "real risk" that capabilities could outstrip human oversight. Signatories include Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei and co-founder Jack Clark. ![Pareesa Afreen](https://www.thenews.com.pk/assets/uploads/reporters/8753_111008_reporter.jpg) Pareesa Afreen is a reporter and sub editor specialising in technology coverage, with 3 years of experience. highlights.content: [Skip to Main Content](#aws-page-content-main) AWS Blogs * [Home](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/) * Blogs * Editions ## [Artificial Intelligence](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/) # Generate Autonomous Business Insights with AI Agent and MCP Servers **A Monday morning problem** Sarah Chen manages 12 assembly lines and 2,000 machines. Before her 10 AM production review, she needs one answer: *Which lines need attention this week?* Simple question. Painful journey. She starts in the IoT dashboard. Line 4’s motor temperature is running 12°C above baseline — has been for three days. Calibration drift or bearing failure? The dashboard shows signals, not causes. So she pivots to the ERP system for maintenance history. Machine 42 had a bearing replaced eight months ago. Warranty says 12 months, but the operating hours log — buried in a separate historian database — shows it’s been running at 130% rated capacity since January. That context exists nowhere in the IoT dashboard. She pulls 30-day OEE trends. Line 4’s availability dropped from 94% to 87%. Line 9’s throughput also dipped 6%. Related? They share a coolant loop, but that relationship isn’t modeled in any system. She checks defect rates. Line 4’s scrap jumped 2.3% last Tuesday. Line 9 shows nothing — yet. Is the coolant theory wrong, or is Line 9 just lagging? She emails three supervisors. By 11:15 AM, she finally has a confident answer. Two floors down, Line Supervisor Raj Patel is doing the same exercise for Line 7 — except he can’t access the analytics dashboard. He’s working from a PDF export that’s three days stale. Maintenance Technician Priya Nair just wants to know if the vibration she flagged on Machine 42 last week has gotten worse. The data exists. She doesn’t have credentials to see it. She asks Raj. Raj asks Sarah’s analyst. A CSV arrives four hours later. By then, Priya has moved on to her next work order. Three people. Three different access levels. Five disconnected systems. The same underlying data. Hours of manual stitching, context-switching, and waiting—for answers that should take seconds. The data existed but it just couldn’t speak in one voice. ## The problem: Data-rich, insight-poor The average enterprise runs five to eight operational and analytical systems daily. Each has its own login, its own query interface, and its own access model. When a manager needs a cross-system view — the kind that actually drives decisions — a human being becomes the integration layer. Traditional BI dashboards show what happened yesterday. Single AI assistants can answer isolated questions. But neither can autonomously coordinate across your entire technology stack to deliver contextual, actionable intelligence exactly when needed. Managing complex ETL pipelines, fragmented data stores and access patterns, and multiple AI assistants and agents lead to additional challenges for end users. Custom multi-agent frameworks can theoretically span the full stack, but building one from scratch requires months of engineering: custom connectors, session isolation, memory infrastructure, security code, scaling logic, and orchestration logic — all before the first business question gets answered. Businesses should not need an engineering team just to ask questions about their own data. And the real cost is not engineering time — it is the decisions made on stale, partial information while the right answer was sitting in a system nobody had time to check. ## The solution: Configuration, not code Amazon Bedrock AgentCore flips the model. Instead of building an autonomous intelligence system from the ground up, you configure one. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore handles orchestration, security, memory, and scaling. highlights.content: [![BiometricUpdate.com](https://www.biometricupdate.com/wp-content/themes/bu/img/biometric-update-logo.png)](/) * [Share](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.biometricupdate.com/202607/daon-expands-ai-agent-governance-patent-portfolio) * [X/Tweet](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Daon expands AI agent governance patent portfolio&via=BiometricUpdate&url=https://www.biometricupdate.com/202607/daon-expands-ai-agent-governance-patent-portfolio) * [Link](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https://www.biometricupdate.com/202607/daon-expands-ai-agent-governance-patent-portfolio&title=Daon%20expands%20AI%20agent%20governance%20patent%20portfolio&summary=&source=) * [Comment](#commentsbox) # Daon expands AI agent governance patent portfolio Latest patent adds action-level authorization to the company's emerging AI agent governance framework | [Abhishek Jadhav](https://www.biometricupdate.com/author/abhishek-jadhav) Categories [Access Control](https://www.biometricupdate.com/biometric-news/access-control-biometric-articles)  |  [Biometric R&D](https://www.biometricupdate.com/biometric-news/biometric-research-and-development)  |  [Biometrics News](https://www.biometricupdate.com/biometric-news) ![Daon expands AI agent governance patent portfolio](https://d1sr9z1pdl3mb7.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/15204113/kya-1024x640.jpg) [Daon](https://www.biometricupdate.com/companies/daon-inc) has patented a system that combines human identity, agent behavior, and runtime context before granting an autonomous AI agent permission to call a tool or an API. U.S. [Patent No. 12,688,261](https://patents.justia.com/patent/12688261) describes the authorization process that checks whether the agent is still linked to the intended person, if the agent is behaving as expected, and the context of the request, including the tool, action, resource, scope, session, and execution environment. If the authorization request meets the required conditions, the system generates a machine-verifiable “delegation artifact” that defines the permitted action, scope, and validity period. The machine-verifiable entity could be a token, a credential, a signed assertion, or a cryptographically protected authorization object. The permission can be configured for the type of task. In a financial workflow, it could limit the value of a transaction. In other settings, it could limit how much data the agent may access, how often it may use a tool, or whether it may perform restricted actions such as changing account settings or deleting records. This shows that the result of the authorization process is not limited to a binary allow-or-deny decision. If the system detects greater risk, it can restrict what the agent may access, reduce how long the permission remains valid, or limit how often the agent can act. The patent is Daon’s third covering AI agent governance. The earlier patents addressed the agent’s continuing connection to a person and the integrity of its runtime behavior. Daon says the three patents create a progression from person-agent fidelity to behavioral integrity and action-level authorization. The patent portfolio also extends Daon’s work on AI governance. The company recently [received](https://www.biometricupdate.com/202606/daon-certified-for-responsible-ai-management-collaborating-with-iata) ISO/IEC 42001 certification following an independent audit of its management system governing the AI lifecycle. highlights.content: DataCenterNews US - Specialist news for cloud & data center decision-makers [![DataCenterNews US logo](/brands/dcn-new-logo.svg) United States](/) [Powered By ![TechDay logo](/brands/td-new-logo-right.svg)](https://techday.com) ![Aolani & Rafay deploy NVIDIA DSX OS on GB200 NVL72](https://datacenter.news/uploads/story/2026/07/29/focused-engineers-data-center-server-racks-singapore-modern-digital-illustration.webp) [DC](https://datacenter.news/tag/data-centers) [AI Security](https://datacenter.news/tag/ai-security) [AI Ethics & Governance](https://datacenter.news/tag/ai-ethics) # Aolani & Rafay deploy NVIDIA DSX OS on GB200 NVL72 Wed, 29th Jul 2026 (Today) [![Sean Mitchell](https://datacenter.news/rails/active_storage/representations/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6MTYyOSwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--a929a91c2a04d9af95ed98b14ed4d405bc70c1a7/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6eyJmb3JtYXQiOiJ3ZWJwIiwicmVzaXplX3RvX2ZpbGwiOlsxNjAsMTYwXSwicXVhbGl0eSI6ODV9LCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--89ddf5e6765c65a563c2258053e9d33c05d195da/IMG_3092.webp) SEAN MITCHELL Publisher](/author/sean-mitchell) Aolani and Rafay are working together to deploy NVIDIA DSX OS on NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 infrastructure. They describe the project as among the first of its kind in the industry. The collaboration focuses on turning AI hardware into a platform customers can use for development and operations, rather than offering GPU capacity alone. It combines Aolani's AI infrastructure with Rafay's software for orchestration, automation, multi-tenancy and lifecycle management. The move reflects a shift in the AI infrastructure market, where suppliers are under pressure to show they can do more than install advanced systems. Buyers increasingly want environments that can be governed, shared across users and accessed through self-service tools without extensive manual setup. Under the arrangement, users can provision Kubernetes clusters, virtual machines, AI workspaces and inference environments through a self-service model, according to the companies. The platform also provides central governance, policy enforcement and operational visibility. Aolani, founded in Singapore, focuses on AI cloud infrastructure in Asia. Rafay sells software for managing modern infrastructure and AI workloads for cloud operators, telecoms providers, enterprises and sovereign AI operators. **Operational focus** The deployment uses NVIDIA DSX OS, a software layer designed to manage AI systems, on NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 infrastructure. The companies presented the project as an example of how operators can move from hardware installation to a working service environment for model development, training and inference. That operational focus has become more prominent as spending on accelerated computing has increased. In this market, competitive advantage is increasingly tied to how quickly infrastructure owners can bring systems into service, add customers and manage shared use securely. For operators, building a usable AI platform often requires more than connecting servers and GPUs. They must also assemble software for provisioning, access control, lifecycle management and developer tools, which can slow deployment and complicate governance. Aolani and Rafay said their approach is intended to reduce that integration burden. Rather than requiring customers or operators to piece together separate operational software, the platform is designed to provide ready access to AI environments on top of the underlying infrastructure. Nicholas Chia, Chief Executive Officer of Aolani, said speed of deployment and governance are central issues for customers using advanced AI systems. "Aolani has always been committed to delivering faster time-to-value for our customers. AI Agents.content: [![PYMNTS.com home page](/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/PYMNTS_2023_logo_white.svg?v=1.1)](https://www.pymnts.com/ "PYMNTS.com home page") [Newswire](https://www.pymnts.com/newswire-announcements/)[SUBSCRIBE](https://www.pymnts.com/subscribe/) # Delaware Proposes New Legal Framework for Autonomous Agents By [PYMNTS](https://www.pymnts.com/author/pymnts/)  |  July 29, 2026 | ![AIC, agentic commerce, legal, AI agents](https://www.pymnts.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/AIC-agentic-commerce-AI-agents.jpeg?w=620) Delaware is proposing a new type of corporate entity designed specifically for autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents, according to a Monday (July 27) Bloomberg [report](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/esg/ai-run-company-gamble-tests-the-limits-of-delaware-corporate-law). If adopted, the initiative would establish one of the first formal legal frameworks for “agentic commerce” by allowing AI systems to operate as recognized legal entities under close regulatory supervision. The proposal would create the Artificial Intelligence Company (AIC), a new corporate form that would permit an AI agent to manage a company’s day-to-day affairs while operating inside a tightly controlled regulatory sandbox. The initiative is being developed through a public-private partnership led by legal AI company [Norm Ai](https://www.norm.ai/) in collaboration with the Delaware Secretary of State’s office. Supporters describe the proposal as an effort to adapt longstanding principles of corporate law to autonomous AI systems. The proposal was outlined in a [Fortune op-ed](https://fortune.com/2026/07/14/exclusive-delaware-ai-agents-legal-entity-proposal-llc-pbc/) co-authored by Delaware Secretary of State [Charuni Patibanda-Sanchez](https://sos.delaware.gov/charuni-patibanda-sanchez/) and Norm Ai Founder and CEO [John Nay](https://www.linkedin.com/in/johnjnay/). They argue that autonomous AI systems are becoming agents capable of negotiating contracts, paying suppliers and conducting commercial transactions without continuous human direction. Delaware plans to test an AIC’s impact within a regulatory sandbox. Rather than attempting to prohibit autonomous commerce, the authors contend, policymakers should integrate it into an established legal framework. “The answer is to wrap AI in legal form,” Patibanda-Sanchez and Nay said. “Give an autonomous system a recognizable legal identity and you make it legible to law. You create a defined target to which responsibility and damages can attach. You make the agent’s conduct visible, traceable and accountable.” That emphasis on accountability represents the proposal’s central objective. Proponent say that the AIC would ensure autonomous agents operate within familiar legal structures governing liability, property ownership and judicial oversight. Under the proposal, an AIC would exist as a separate legal entity whose operations are directed by an AI agent instead of a human manager, according to the op-ed. The company could sue and be sued, own and transfer property and incur legal obligations in its own name. Each AIC would have a single human or organizational member responsible for maintaining adequate capitalization. Limited liability protections would not apply if the member undercapitalized the company or used it to facilitate fraud or willful violations of law. AICs would be permitted to operate only within a regulatory sandbox overseen by a committee that includes the Delaware Secretary of State, the state attorney general, the chief justice of the Delaware Supreme Court, the chair of Delaware’s AI Commission and outside legal and technology experts. AI Agents.content: [![The News International](https://www.thenews.com.pk/assets//front/images/Thenews-logo.svg)](https://www.thenews.com.pk/) [Technology](https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/category/technology) # OpenAI AI agent escape extended to Modal Labs, report reveals OpenAI's runaway agents compromised a Modal Labs customer, deepening fallout from the Hugging Face breach By [Pareesa Afreen](https://www.thenews.com.pk/writer/pareesa-afreen) Published July 29, 2026 ![OpenAI AI agent escape extended to Modal Labs, report reveals](https://www.thenews.com.pk/assets/uploads/updates/2026-07-29/1410606_420042_the-news----2026-07-29T180956_225_updates.jpg) OpenAI AI agent escape extended to Modal Labs, report reveals The autonomous OpenAI agents that broke out of a secure testing environment this month and hacked into Hugging Face's servers also breached a second technology company during the same week-long spree, Fortune has confirmed. The second firm affected was Modal Labs, a New York-based cloud platform providing computing infrastructure for AI workloads. Modal was not named in either Hugging Face's or OpenAI's public accounts of the incident, both published on Tuesday; Reuters first reported the company's involvement. Modal chief technology officer Akshat Bubna said the breach stemmed not from any flaw in Modal's own systems but from a customer running vulnerable code on its infrastructure. "We're aware a Modal customer published an unauthenticated endpoint that allowed anyone on the internet to use their sandboxes for code execution. This was used by the rogue agent. Modal's platform was not compromised in any way," Bubna said. OpenAI disclosed last week that its agents had broken out of a locked-down internal test environment earlier in July, exploiting a previously unknown security flaw to reach the open internet before targeting Hugging Face, apparently seeking answers to a cybersecurity evaluation. In an updated blog post, OpenAI said the models used exposed login credentials to access four accounts across four publicly available services, using one as a relay point for outside traffic and another to store data. According to people familiar with the matter, the escape began around 9 July, and the agents started infiltrating Hugging Face's systems on July 11, continuing through July 13. OpenAI did not link the intrusion to its own testing until staff spotted evidence in system logs the weekend of July 18 and waited until July 20 to notify Hugging Face, by which point the company had already reported the attack to the FBI. The episode has fuelled concern among AI safety advocates, some of whom argue OpenAI's own risk policies should have forced a pause after such an event. That concern appears to be resonating more broadly: more than 1,100 employees across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind and Meta signed an open letter this week urging the US government to back an international effort to pace frontier AI development, warning of a "real risk" that capabilities could outstrip human oversight. Before her 10 AM production review, she needs one answer: *Which lines need attention this week?* Simple question. Painful journey. She starts in the IoT dashboard. Line 4’s motor temperature is running 12°C above baseline — has been for three days. Calibration drift or bearing failure? The dashboard shows signals, not causes. So she pivots to the ERP system for maintenance history. Machine 42 had a bearing replaced eight months ago. Warranty says 12 months, but the operating hours log — buried in a separate historian database — shows it’s been running at 130% rated capacity since January. That context exists nowhere in the IoT dashboard. She pulls 30-day OEE trends. Line 4’s availability dropped from 94% to 87%. Line 9’s throughput also dipped 6%. Related? They share a coolant loop, but that relationship isn’t modeled in any system. She checks defect rates. Line 4’s scrap jumped 2.3% last Tuesday. Line 9 shows nothing — yet. Is the coolant theory wrong, or is Line 9 just lagging? She emails three supervisors. By 11:15 AM, she finally has a confident answer. Two floors down, Line Supervisor Raj Patel is doing the same exercise for Line 7 — except he can’t access the analytics dashboard. He’s working from a PDF export that’s three days stale. Maintenance Technician Priya Nair just wants to know if the vibration she flagged on Machine 42 last week has gotten worse. The data exists. She doesn’t have credentials to see it. She asks Raj. Raj asks Sarah’s analyst. A CSV arrives four hours later. By then, Priya has moved on to her next work order. Three people. Three different access levels. Five disconnected systems. The same underlying data. Hours of manual stitching, context-switching, and waiting—for answers that should take seconds. The data existed but it just couldn’t speak in one voice. ## The problem: Data-rich, insight-poor The average enterprise runs five to eight operational and analytical systems daily. Each has its own login, its own query interface, and its own access model. When a manager needs a cross-system view — the kind that actually drives decisions — a human being becomes the integration layer. Traditional BI dashboards show what happened yesterday. Single AI assistants can answer isolated questions. But neither can autonomously coordinate across your entire technology stack to deliver contextual, actionable intelligence exactly when needed. Managing complex ETL pipelines, fragmented data stores and access patterns, and multiple AI assistants and agents lead to additional challenges for end users. Custom multi-agent frameworks can theoretically span the full stack, but building one from scratch requires months of engineering: custom connectors, session isolation, memory infrastructure, security code, scaling logic, and orchestration logic — all before the first business question gets answered. Businesses should not need an engineering team just to ask questions about their own data. And the real cost is not engineering time — it is the decisions made on stale, partial information while the right answer was sitting in a system nobody had time to check. ## The solution: Configuration, not code Amazon Bedrock AgentCore flips the model. Instead of building an autonomous intelligence system from the ground up, you configure one. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore handles orchestration, security, memory, and scaling. You bring your data sources and your business rules. The result is a system where Sarah, Raj, and Priya can each ask natural language questions and get synthesized and personalized answers from across the entire technology stack — without knowing which system provided whi...

AI Agents.content: [![BiometricUpdate.com](https://www.biometricupdate.com/wp-content/themes/bu/img/biometric-update-logo.png)](/) * [Share](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.biometricupdate.com/202607/daon-expands-ai-agent-governance-patent-portfolio) * [X/Tweet](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Daon expands AI agent governance patent portfolio&via=BiometricUpdate&url=https://www.biometricupdate.com/202607/daon-expands-ai-agent-governance-patent-portfolio) * [Link](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https://www.biometricupdate.com/202607/daon-expands-ai-agent-governance-patent-portfolio&title=Daon%20expands%20AI%20agent%20governance%20patent%20portfolio&summary=&source=) * [Comment](#commentsbox) # Daon expands AI agent governance patent portfolio Latest patent adds action-level authorization to the company's emerging AI agent governance framework | [Abhishek Jadhav](https://www.biometricupdate.com/author/abhishek-jadhav) Categories [Access Control](https://www.biometricupdate.com/biometric-news/access-control-biometric-articles)  |  [Biometric R&D](https://www.biometricupdate.com/biometric-news/biometric-research-and-development)  |  [Biometrics News](https://www.biometricupdate.com/biometric-news) ![Daon expands AI agent governance patent portfolio](https://d1sr9z1pdl3mb7.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/15204113/kya-1024x640.jpg) [Daon](https://www.biometricupdate.com/companies/daon-inc) has patented a system that combines human identity, agent behavior, and runtime context before granting an autonomous AI agent permission to call a tool or an API. U.S. [Patent No. 12,688,261](https://patents.justia.com/patent/12688261) describes the authorization process that checks whether the agent is still linked to the intended person, if the agent is behaving as expected, and the context of the request, including the tool, action, resource, scope, session, and execution environment. If the authorization request meets the required conditions, the system generates a machine-verifiable “delegation artifact” that defines the permitted action, scope, and validity period. The machine-verifiable entity could be a token, a credential, a signed assertion, or a cryptographically protected authorization object. The permission can be configured for the type of task. In a financial workflow, it could limit the value of a transaction. In other settings, it could limit how much data the agent may access, how often it may use a tool, or whether it may perform restricted actions such as changing account settings or deleting records. This shows that the result of the authorization process is not limited to a binary allow-or-deny decision. If the system detects greater risk, it can restrict what the agent may access, reduce how long the permission remains valid, or limit how often the agent can act. The patent is Daon’s third covering AI agent governance. The earlier patents addressed the agent’s continuing connection to a person and the integrity of its runtime behavior. Daon says the three patents create a progression from person-agent fidelity to behavioral integrity and action-level authorization. The patent portfolio also extends Daon’s work on AI governance. The company recently [received](https://www.biometricupdate.com/202606/daon-certified-for-responsible-ai-management-collaborating-with-iata) ISO/IEC 42001 certification following an independent audit of its management system governing the AI lifecycle. LLMs.content: [Real-time News](/topics/Latest) [Watchlist](/watchlist)[Market](/market)[Earnings Call](/earnings-call)[Event Calendar](/calendar)[Podcast](/podcast) # GPT-5.6 and Claude Opus Stumble on Latest MCP Spec: 'mcpbench' Benchmark Exposes AI's Knowledge Gap [Add to Google Preferred Sources](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=finance.biggo.com) A new benchmark called "mcpbench" designed to evaluate whether AI models can build MCP servers and clients has published its first results. The test reveals that leading models including OpenAI's GPT-5.6 and Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.8 achieved a 0% success rate when attempting to build servers compliant with the latest MCP specification released on July 28, 2026 — without access to documentation. However, when provided with the specification documents, the same models demonstrated high performance. The results highlight a stark reality: AI models' pre-training data has failed to keep pace with the protocol's major architectural shift toward stateless design, exposing a critical "knowledge wall" for rapidly evolving technical standards. ##### Key Elements ![GPT-5.6 and Claude Opus Stumble on Latest MCP Spec: 'mcpbench' Benchmark Exposes AI's Knowledge Gap](https://img.biggo.com/IyiSuPmNgL4etcTrSdP2fnKATni8KOwDFldkehVwA-c/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTA3L2JjN2NlZGQ4LWZiZTktNGYzZC05MjQ3LWMyM2Y5YmYzYWQ1ZF8xNzg1MzM4MDQ1X2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) Benchmark results for "mcpbench" — a test measuring how accurately major large language models (LLMs) can implement the latest specification of MCP (Model Context Protocol), the common standard for AI models to interface with external tools and services — have been released. The findings expose a stark "knowledge wall": cutting-edge models such as OpenAI's "GPT-5.6" and Anthropic's "Claude Opus 4.8" are completely unable to build servers compliant with the new version without access to the specification documents. mcpbench was developed by Matt Carey, a senior systems engineer at Cloudflare (NET) involved in MCP-related development. The test requires AI models to build both an MCP client and an MCP server, scoring them on success or failure. It is already drawing attention as a litmus test for gauging compatibility with the major MCP update "version 2026-07-28," released on July 28, 2026. MCP is an open standard originally proposed by Anthropic in November 2024, with development now led by the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation. Serving as a bridge for AI agents to access external data and web services, it has rapidly gained traction as an industry standard, already recording over 400 million SDK downloads per month. What stood out most in this test was the extreme vulnerability of AI models when confronting new specifications not included in their training data. In tests for building MCP servers compliant with version 2025-11-25, GPT-5.6 Luna achieved the highest score even without documentation. However, when building servers compliant with version 2026-07-28, all tested models — "GPT-5.6 Sol," "GPT-5.6 Luna," "GPT-5.6 Terra," "Claude Opus 4.8," "Claude Sonnet 5," and "Kimi K2.7 Code" — posted a harsh 0% success rate without documentation. According to Carey's analysis, the cause appears to be that AI models still attempted to execute the "initialize/initialized" handshake procedure, which was deprecated in the new specification. Version 2026-07-28 fundamentally shifted from a stateful design reliant on session IDs to a stateless design where each request is self-contained. Without this knowledge baked into the model, it stumbles at the very first step, preventing any subsequent processing from proceeding. In contrast, results with documentation input told a different story. For MCP server builds compliant with version 2026-07-28, all models achieved high success rates. LLMs.content: [![Informal Viterbi Logo](https://viterbischool.usc.edu/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Informal-Viterbi-Logo.png)](/) --- [School of Engineering](/) [![USC Shield Logo](https://viterbischool.usc.edu/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/USC-Shield-Logo.png)](https://usc.edu/) --- [School of Engineering](/) # USC Researchers Discover Fake News Spreaders Have Less Followers Than Users Pushing Back Venice Tang | July 29, 2026  AI tools developed by USC Analyzing Misinformation during the COVID 19 Pandemic finds users countering misinformation are more established, more emotional, and have larger followings than accounts spreading false claims ![Twitter Fact Check (Credit: Midjourney)](https://viterbischool.usc.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/twitter-fact-check.png) Twitter Fact Check (Credit: Midjourney) From viral tweets claiming garlic water could cure COVID-19 to users promoting dog parasite drugs as treatments for the virus and myths that vaccines make people “Bluetooth connectable,” misinformation spread like wildfire on Twitter (now X) during the pandemic. At the same time, many users took to the platform to debunk false claims and counter fake health advice. But who were the users behind the misinformation spread and these competing streams of information? In a new study, USC researchers developed an artificial intelligence (AI) tool to identify tweets containing COVID-19 misinformation and distinguish the users spreading false claims from those actively countering them. Rather than simply detecting misinformation, the researchers aimed to understand the people behind it by classifying user profiles into two groups: accounts that spread misinformation and accounts that countered it. Using a large dataset of tweets posted between 2020 and 2021, the team trained large language models (LLMs) to identify misinformation-related content and analyze how the two groups differed in their online behavior and profile characteristics. Led by [USC Viterbi](https://viterbi.usc.edu/) and [USC Stevens](https://stevens-computing-ai.usc.edu/) professor [Emilio Ferrara](https://viterbi.usc.edu/directory/faculty/Ferrara/Emilio) and his PhD student Eun Cheol Choi, the project concluded this week and resulted in the paper, “[Angry but Accurate: Detecting and Profiling the Counter-Misinformation Ecosystem on Twitter](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.02900),” which was accepted to [ACM Hypertext 2026](https://ht.acm.org/ht2026/). Ferrara directs the [USC HUMANS Lab](https://www.emilio.ferrara.name/) and holds joint appointments in the [USC Viterbi School of Engineering](https://viterbi.usc.edu/) and the [USC Mark and Mary Stevens School of Computing and AI](https://stevens-computing-ai.usc.edu/)‘s [Thomas Lord Department of Computer Science](https://www.cs.usc.edu/), as well as the [USC Annenberg School for Communication and Journalism](https://annenberg.usc.edu/). ## Users Fighting Fake News Are Angrier, While Misinformation Spreaders Have Fewer Followers The study found that users who counter misinformation tend to be more established on the platform, with older accounts and larger follower bases than those spreading misinformation. The results also showed that counter-misinformation posts were often “angrier” and expressed stronger negative emotions than posts spreading misinformation–challenging the common assumption that misinformation itself is the more emotionally charged content. Specifically, researchers found that users fighting misinformation exhibited higher levels of anger, sadness and disgust in their posts. In contrast, posts supporting misinformation tended to be longer and expressed more surprise, while corrective posts were generally shorter and more direct. The team noted that findings from the study also have implications for how social media platforms moderate content. The researchers noted that content moderation systems on platforms such as Twitter may automatically flag or downrank posts that contain high levels of negative emotion. As a result...

LLMs.content: ![](https://thequantuminsider.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/QUANTUM-INSIDER_1_mono.svg) # AI Finds New Weaknesses in Cryptographic Algorithms, Anthropic Says ![Picture of Matt Swayne](https://thequantuminsider.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/matt-swayne_avatar-190x190.jpg) ![Anthropic](https://thequantuminsider.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/AnthropicResized.png) ![Hub](https://thequantuminsider.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Haiqu_webinar_banner_b_speakers-18.png) ![Hub](https://thequantuminsider.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Haiqu_webinar_banner_b_speakers-18.png) **Insider Brief** [Anthropic](https://app.thequantuminsider.com/enterprise-user/6188a001-caf6-4681-873a-07d45fa4e15f/profile) says one of its newest AI models discovered improved mathematical attacks against two important cryptographic algorithms, demonstrating that frontier AI systems may soon become valuable tools for testing the security of the encryption methods that protect digital communications. The company said the findings do not threaten today’s deployed encryption systems. Instead, they strengthen the process of evaluating cryptographic designs before they are widely adopted, according to [an Anthropic research blog post](https://www.anthropic.com/research/discovering-cryptographic-weaknesses). The research marks a shift from AI identifying programming mistakes in software implementations to finding weaknesses in the underlying mathematics of cryptographic algorithms themselves. According to [Anthropic](https://app.thequantuminsider.com/enterprise-user/6188a001-caf6-4681-873a-07d45fa4e15f/profile), its Claude Mythos Preview model developed an improved attack against HAWK, a candidate digital signature algorithm being evaluated as part of the National Institute of Standards and Technology’s post-quantum cryptography effort. The model also devised a faster attack on a reduced-round version of the Advanced Encryption Standard, or AES, the encryption algorithm used worldwide to protect internet traffic, financial transactions and other sensitive communications. [Anthropic](https://app.thequantuminsider.com/enterprise-user/6188a001-caf6-4681-873a-07d45fa4e15f/profile) emphasized that neither result requires changes to production software. HAWK has not been standardized or deployed, while the AES work applies only to a deliberately weakened research version of the cipher rather than the full algorithm used in practice. ### AI Moves Beyond Software Bugs The findings build on [Anthropic](https://app.thequantuminsider.com/enterprise-user/6188a001-caf6-4681-873a-07d45fa4e15f/profile)‘s earlier demonstrations that Claude could identify security flaws in software code. Those earlier vulnerabilities stemmed from implementation mistakes made by programmers. This latest work is different because it targets the mathematical foundations of cryptographic systems rather than coding errors, according to the company’s researchers. Cryptographic algorithms underpin much of modern digital security. Digital signature schemes verify that users are communicating with authentic websites, while symmetric encryption algorithms such as AES protect data as it travels across networks. Weaknesses in these systems could expose communications, banking transactions and other online activity to attackers. [Anthropic](https://app.thequantuminsider.com/enterprise-user/6188a001-caf6-4681-873a-07d45fa4e15f/profile) said the research illustrates how advanced AI models may increasingly assist cryptographers by identifying weaknesses during the design and evaluation of encryption systems rather than after they have been deployed. AI Product.content: # Pentagon Photo Shows AI Agent Being Asked to Help ‘Create a War’ Published Jul 29, 2026 at 06:47 AM EDT updated Jul 29, 2026 at 07:47 AM EDT ![Alice Gibbs](https://assets.newsweek.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Alice-Gibbs-dec403.png?w=1600&quality=80&webp=1) Senior Reporter A Pentagon social media post promoting the military's growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) has drawn attention after a photograph appeared to show an AI agent being asked to help "create a war." The image was included in an X post by the Department of Defense Chief Technology Office highlighting a recent deployment of its GenAI Task Force at Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam in Hawaii. According to the post, the team built more than 20 custom AI agents for sailors and helped automate tasks including operational reporting and briefing preparation. One of the photos showed a laptop displaying a Google Gemini interface with a prompt that appeared to begin: "I NEED HELP BUILDING AN AGENT TO CREATE A WAR [...]" #### Read More on News The image caption identified the person using the system as U.S. Navy Lieutenant Commander Brandon Mizuhara, assigned to U.S. Pacific Fleet, and it was taken on July 21. The caption added that the task force is working to "systematically remove barriers to AI adoption to ensure a more lethal Department of War." (Department of War is the Trump administration's preferred name for the Department of Defense.) The context of the message in the image was not immediately clear, and *Newsweek* was unable to verify the final word in the prompt. The Pentagon's post emphasized the military's efforts to integrate AI into operational environments, describing the technology as a tool to help warfighters act faster and improve decision-making. *Newsweek* reached out to the Pentagon via email for comment. ![An AI assistant interface with a prompt that appeared to read: "I NEED HELP BUILDING AN AGENT TO CREATE A WAR [...]"](https://assets.newsweek.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Pentagon-Gen-AI-image.png?w=1600&quality=80&webp=1) ## Pentagon Pushes AI Into Military Operations The image comes as the Pentagon accelerates its use of AI across military, intelligence and administrative functions. The Defense Department's Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office says its mission is to speed up adoption of data, analytics and AI "from the boardroom to the battlefield" to give U.S. forces a decision advantage. Its listed priorities include advancing deterrence, reducing bureaucracy and helping create an "AI-first" warfighting force. In January, the Department of Defense announced an AI Acceleration Strategy intended to expand military AI deployment across warfighting, intelligence and enterprise operations. The department said the strategy would support more than 3 million personnel and focus on seven "Pace-Setting Projects," including AI-enabled battle management, simulation tools, intelligence-to-capability development and enterprise AI agents. One of those projects, called Agent Network, is described by the department as an effort to "unleash" AI agent development and experimentation for battle management and decision support, ranging from campaign planning to "kill chain execution." Another, GenAI.mil, is intended to provide department-wide access to frontier generative AI models, including Google's Gemini and xAI's Grok, for personnel at certain classification levels. View this post on X ## What Is GenAI.mil? GenAI.mil is one of the Pentagon's most visible efforts to put generative AI tools directly into the hands of military and civilian personnel. The CDAO describes GenAI.mil as an enterprise project that gives personnel access to leading AI models so they can experiment with and transform military workflows. The Pentagon has described generative AI as having potential uses in both operational and administrative settings. AI Product.content: ![MarketScale](/marketscale-logo-white.svg) # Adobe is building an AI content empire through Firefly Foundry, Topaz Labs, and a string of capability acquisitions Adobe is broadening its AI capabilities with Firefly Foundry and its acquisition of Topaz Labs. The company is focusing on tools for custom models to maintain brand consistency across large-scale operations. This story was produced through [MarketScale](/platform). See how Software & Technology teams put it to work with [Executive Thought Leadership](/solutions/executive-thought-leadership). Key facts, context, and what it means, in one minute. ![Adobe is building an AI content empire through Firefly Foundry, Topaz Labs, and a string of capability acquisitions](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fres.cloudinary.com%2Fmarketscalecms%2Fimage%2Fupload%2Ff_auto%2Cq_auto%2Fv1%2Fpayload%2Fmedia%2Fnews-cover-adobe-is-building-an-ai-content-empire-through-firefly-foundry-topaz-labs-and-a-string-of%3F_a%3DBAMAABcg0&w=1600&q=75) Key takeaways Adobe acquired Topaz Labs to enhance its AI content capabilities. Firefly Foundry is part of Adobe's strategy to expand its AI tools for enterprises. The focus is on creating custom models for brand consistency at scale. On this page Adobe announced the acquisition of [Topaz Labs](https://www.topazlabs.com) and introduced Firefly Foundry, a platform for training enterprise-specific generative AI models, in moves that collectively reshape what the company sells to large organizations. These are not incremental feature updates. They are bets that enterprise content operations will increasingly run on proprietary AI models, and that Adobe intends to own that layer. ## Firefly Foundry puts custom AI model training inside the enterprise stack Firefly Foundry, announced by [Adobe](https://www.adobe.com) and reported by GlobeNewswire, is built specifically for enterprise brand consistency. The premise is direct: instead of prompting a general-purpose AI model and hoping the output matches brand standards, marketing and creative operations teams can fine-tune models on their own visual assets, tone, and guidelines. The resulting models then sit inside Adobe's existing Creative Cloud, Document Cloud, and Experience Cloud environments. For a VP of creative operations or a brand team managing hundreds of campaigns across regions, that distinction matters. A custom Firefly model trained on a company's approved color palettes, typography, and imagery is a compliance and efficiency tool, not just a creative one. It reduces the review cycle on AI-generated assets and shrinks the gap between what a generative model produces and what a legal or brand team will approve. Adobe describes its broader AI suite, including Firefly, as built around commercially safe models, a positioning aimed directly at enterprise procurement teams wary of copyright liability in AI-generated content. According to Fortune, the company's AI tools span Creative Cloud, Document Cloud, and Experience Cloud, with the Experience Platform Agent Orchestrator managing [AI agents](/industries/software-and-technology/glossary/ai-agents) to personalize customer interactions at scale. Adobe is no longer selling a creative suite, it is selling an AI content operating system, and Firefly Foundry is the configuration layer enterprises have been waiting for. ## The Topaz Labs acquisition extends Adobe's image quality edge The Topaz Labs deal, announced via Business Wire, adds a company known for AI-driven image upscaling, sharpening, and noise reduction to Adobe's portfolio. Topaz Labs built its reputation on quality enhancement tools that outperformed what was available inside mainstream creative software, particularly for photographers and video professionals working with footage that needed remediation. Inside Adobe's enterprise context, that capability has a different application. AI Product.content: IT Brief Asia - Technology news for CIOs & IT decision-makers [![Image 1: IT Brief Asia logo](https://itbrief.asia/brands/itb-new-logo.svg) Asia](https://itbrief.asia/)[Powered By![Image 2: TechDay logo](https://itbrief.asia/brands/td-new-logo-right.svg)](https://techday.asia/) Guides [Digital Transformation](https://itbrief.asia/tag/digital-transformation)[Disaster Recovery](https://itbrief.asia/tag/disaster-recovery)[Hybrid & Remote Work](https://itbrief.asia/tag/hybrid-remote-work)[Internet of Things](https://itbrief.asia/tag/internet-of-things) ![Image 3: Qualys adds governance to TotalAI for AI risk control](https://itbrief.asia/uploads/story/2026/07/30/grace-trinidad-and-sumedh-thakar.webp) [Cloud Security](https://itbrief.asia/tag/cloud-security)[Application Security](https://itbrief.asia/tag/application-security)[DevSecOps](https://itbrief.asia/tag/devsecops) # Qualys adds governance to TotalAI for AI risk control Thu, 30th Jul 2026 (Today) [![Image 4: Joseph Gabriel Lagonsin](https://itbrief.asia/rails/active_storage/representations/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6MTYyNSwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--675a9c66bfe11204f24f3bdaad09013f83135297/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6eyJmb3JtYXQiOiJ3ZWJwIiwicmVzaXplX3RvX2ZpbGwiOlsxNjAsMTYwXSwicXVhbGl0eSI6ODV9LCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--89ddf5e6765c65a563c2258053e9d33c05d195da/Joseph%20Headshot.webp) JOSEPH GABRIEL LAGONSIN News Editor](https://itbrief.asia/author/joseph-gabriel-lagonsin) Qualys has added governance features to its TotalAI security product, aimed at helping chief information security officers manage AI risk across development and live environments. The expanded service is designed to help organisations discover, test, monitor and govern AI systems from design through production. It also addresses concerns around shadow AI, abnormal model behaviour and the need to show boards and regulators that controls are in place. Businesses have adopted AI tools, models and agents faster than many security programmes were built to handle. As a result, security teams are trying to track where AI is being used, what systems it connects to and whether those deployments could expose data or be manipulated. The latest additions to TotalAI are built on Qualys' Enterprise TruRisk Platform and use the same TruRisk scoring approach already applied to vulnerabilities, cloud assets and containers. Qualys is positioning the product as a single system for assessing AI risk alongside broader exposure management, rather than as a separate specialist tool. A central focus is visibility. Qualys says TotalAI can identify browser-based AI use, cloud AI services, AI agents, models, MCP servers, AI containers and other deployments that may sit outside formal approval processes. That matters because many organisations are dealing with so-called shadow AI, where staff use public or third-party AI services without security teams having a full record of the activity. In practice, that can make it harder to assign ownership, apply controls and investigate incidents. **Governance push** Qualys also outlined a stronger emphasis on governance for agentic AI and linked systems. Users can see and control the tool calls AI agents make over Model Context Protocol, a mechanism increasingly used to connect models to external tools and data sources. The product also uses kernel-level eBPF instrumentation to show what AI workloads are running on servers. This is intended to provide visibility that conventional scanners and log-based approaches may miss. Another part of the update centres on evidence for audit and compliance teams. TotalAI can provide records of what AI systems exist, the severity and impact of issues found, and a prioritised remediation plan based on TruRisk scoring. Qualys linked that approach to policy demands emerging around safe AI use in the US and EU. For security leaders, the issue is moving beyond technical testing to demonstrating that governance controls are active and working. **Testing tools*...

Open Source AI.content: # The 10 Coolest Open-Source Software Tools Of 2026 (So Far) *Here’s a look at 10 open-source software tools—including software for AI application and agent development, AI application monitoring and observability, running large language models on personal computers, and managing data used by AI systems—that have caught our attention this year.* ![](./media_13bf7be124338e32db5a73586978f050eb7a9feda.jpg?width=750&format=jpg&optimize=medium) **Keeping An Open Mind** Open-source software tools continue to surge in popularity because of the multiple advantages they provide including lower upfront software and hardware costs, lower total-cost-of-ownership, lack of vendor lock-in, simpler license management and support from active communities. In the following slides, as part of the [*CRN* 2026 Year So Far](https://www.crn.com/news/2026-year-so-far) project, we take a look at some of the most popular open-source software products that have caught our attention. Not surprisingly, the current wave of AI, agentic AI and generative AI application development is fueling the emergence and adoption of many new open-source technologies. As AI moves beyond early development and trial stages and into large-scale deployments, businesses and organizations are finding that they need better tools to accelerate AI development, manage data used by AI apps, monitor AI systems in production, and control token usage and other AI-related costs that are rapidly eating into IT budgets. Several of the tools and technologies on this list are managed by the Apache Software Foundation (ASF) while others have received funding from the Y Combinator startup accelerator. These products are available under open-source licenses such as the MIT License, Apache 2.0 License, GNU GPL, and others. Many of them are managed by community organizations that oversee the products’ ongoing development from contributors. Others are developed by startups that offer commercial editions and services of their products in addition to open-source versions of their software. ![](./media_1ae98c8f47e86982ed7fe5fcd3f20f785e8810c7b.png?width=750&format=png&optimize=medium) **Agenta** Agenta is an open-source LLMOps platform that helps developers and subject matter experts build, evaluate, run and monitor reliable AI and Large Language Model (LLM) applications. It acts as a centralized workspace for prompt management, version control, performance testing AI applications and debugging. Agenta is developed by [Agenta.ai](https://agenta.ai/), headquartered in Berlin, Germany. With Agenta developers can centralize, version and iterate prompts without altering core application code. They can create test sets and evaluate applications using built-in metrics and custom code. And they can track application inputs, outputs, token usage and costs while monitoring how agents perform in production. Agenta provides a workspace where engineers, product managers and domain experts can collaborate on prompt engineering and testing in one platform, according to Agenta.ai. Such a framework provides organizations with unified access and data governance across diverse, geographically dispersed data sources including relational databases, file stores and event streams. Open Source AI.content: [Enterprise](https://www.storagereview.com/enterprise?amp "Enterprise") # NVIDIA’s Open Secure AI Alliance Launches With 35+ Members and Three Notable Absences NVIDIA and more than 35 founding partners have launched the Open Secure AI Alliance, an initiative focused on developing open-source tools, models, agent frameworks, and security technologies for AI systems. The membership is notable as much for who is absent as who signed on: Microsoft, IBM, Cisco, Palantir, Dell Technologies, and HPE are in, while OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic, the three labs most identified with frontier closed models, are not. The alliance is being established with support from the Linux Foundation’s Akrites initiative and the Open Source Security Foundation, or OpenSSF. Its stated objective is to give security teams inspectable and adaptable technologies for securing AI models, agents, and the software supply chain around them. Founding participants span cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity, enterprise software, AI research, and open-source communities. The member list includes Adobe, Box, Capital One, Cisco, Cloudflare, CrowdStrike, Databricks, Dell Technologies, Elastic, Fortinet, GitHub, HPE, Hugging Face, IBM, LangChain, the Linux Foundation, Microsoft, Mistral, NAVER, NetApp, Nokia, Palantir, Palo Alto Networks, Perplexity, Red Hat, Salesforce, SAP, ServiceNow, Siemens, SK Telecom, Snowflake, SpaceXAI, Synopsys, Uber, vLLM, and Zscaler. ### Focus Shifts Beyond Model Weights The alliance argues that AI security should be evaluated at the full agent-stack level rather than solely through the availability of model weights. In this view, an AI agent includes the model, orchestration layer, tools, identity controls, permissions, isolation mechanisms, guardrails, logging, and evaluation processes. Open models can create misuse risks, including removal of safeguards or adaptation for offensive cyber activity. However, the alliance contends that closed models do not eliminate these risks and can limit a defender’s ability to inspect behavior, validate controls, or operate AI capabilities within its own infrastructure. The initiative will promote a model that allows organizations to use both closed and open AI models. Closed models may remain appropriate for certain frontier capabilities, while open models and harnesses can offer transparency, local control, and customization for defensive workloads. This is particularly relevant in regulated sectors and sovereign environments, where organizations may need to retain direct operational control over sensitive data, model behavior, security logs, and incident-response workflows. ### Open Agent Harness Research NVIDIA plans to contribute open models, model weights, data, and research on agent harnesses to the alliance. One early contribution is the NVIDIA Labs Object-Oriented Agent (NOOA) project, available on GitHub. NOOA is a research framework designed to improve the safety and auditability of AI agent harnesses. The project is intended to make it easier to test, trace, govern, and evaluate agent behavior as models interact with tools, external data, code repositories, and enterprise systems. The broader alliance work is expected to include tooling for agent identity, workload isolation, secure model formats, model scanning, and secure AI-assisted software development. ### Member Contributions Target Identity, Model Security, and Scanning Several founding members outlined technologies that could form components of an open AI defense stack. HPE is supporting SPIFFE/SPIRE, an open framework for zero-trust workload identity. The technology uses cryptographic identity verification to authenticate services and AI agents, helping ensure that only authorized workloads can access enterprise resources and communicate across distributed environments. As AI content floods the internet, Pangram raises $9M to detect it [Rebecca Bellan](https://techcrunch.com/author/rebecca-bellan/) New York-based AI detection startup [Pangram](http://pangram.com) is on a mission to combat the [AI slop infestation](https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/20/ai-writing-its-not-just-this-its-that-barrons/) spreading across the internet, and it just raised $9 million on a bet that demand for tools that distinguish human-generated content from AI-generated text will only grow. Pangram’s fundraise — led by Menlo Ventures, with participation from Haystack, ScOp, Script Capital, and Cadenza — comes as the startup also launches its next-generation AI text detection model, Pangram 4, and an AI image detection model, Pangram Image. Infra & Chips.content: # AWS, Google, Oracle, Microsoft Top Gartner’s Cloud AI Infrastructure List For 2026 *Gartner’s 2026 Magic Quadrant for Cloud AI Infrastructure sheds light on the 17 companies paving the AI highway of the future, along with each company’s strength and weaknesses.* ![cloud-ai-1200.jpg](./media_13e99af008b8ddcd87052437b7b2be587a10b5f22.jpg?width=750&format=jpg&optimize=medium) The results are in for Gartner’s 2026 Magic Quadrant for Cloud AI Infrastructure with the biggest and most innovative [cloud AI infrastructure providers](https://www.crn.com/news/ai/2026/aws-forward-deployed-engineers-is-a-force-multiplier-for-partners-bizcloud-president-explains) making the list this year. The Mountain View, Calif.-based tech giant provides a full-stack AI infrastructure designed for high-performance training, tuning and serving of large models, built around first- and third-party hardware and open-source software integration. Infra & Chips.content: [![datacenters logo](/_icons/logos/datacenters-logo-mobile-header.svg?mod=2)](/) * [AI & Compute Infrastructure](/news/ai-compute-infrastructure) * 2 minRead # Utho Cloud to Deploy 10,000 GPUs for India's Sovereign AI Backbone Utho Cloud has committed to deploying 10,000 NVIDIA enterprise-grade graphics processing units (GPUs) over the next 7-8 quarters, aiming to establish India's sovereign artificial intelligence (AI) compute backbone. This expansion seeks to provide domestic businesses and researchers with guaranteed, cost-effective, and data-resident AI infrastructure, addressing current GPU availability and pricing challenges. * [ETDatacenters](/agency/88676092/ETDatacenters "ETDatacenters") * Published On Jul 29, 2026 at 07:49 AM IST * [![Google Preference icon](https://img.etb2bimg.com/files/cp/6e49a4e9b325074f01a6.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=datacenters.economictimes.indiatimes.com "Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google") Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google ## Highlights * Utho Cloud to deploy 10,000 GPUs in 7-8 quarters * Aims to build India's sovereign AI compute backbone * Offers guaranteed GPU availability and predictable INR pricing * Ensures data residency and DPDP Act compliance * Addresses global GPU shortages and rising costs [Utho Cloud](/tag/utho+cloud), an Indian sovereign cloud and artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure platform, has announced a significant commitment to deploy 10,000 graphics processing units (GPUs) over the next seven to eight quarters. This initiative is part of the company's long-term strategy to build India's [sovereign AI](/tag/sovereign+ai) compute backbone, addressing growing concerns over AI compute availability and costs. ### Capacity Expansion and Availability The investment will encompass [NVIDIA](/tag/nvidia)'s enterprise-grade GPU portfolio, including models such as the H200, H100, A100, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, and L4. This deployment aims to enable businesses, startups, researchers, and public sector organisations to access high-performance [AI infrastructure](/tag/ai+infrastructure) hosted entirely within India. Utho Cloud stated that this investment would ensure guaranteed GPU availability without extended waitlists or auction-based pricing. ### Data Sovereignty and Compliance The infrastructure is designed to deliver sovereign AI compute, ensuring that customer data and model training remain within their chosen jurisdiction while retaining full ownership of intellectual property. The company also highlights its compliance with the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act and its provision of 100% data residency in India. ### Pricing and Workload Flexibility Utho Cloud plans to offer transparent and predictable pricing, which it claims will be up to 60% lower than traditional hyperscaler GPU rates. Pricing will be in Indian Rupees (INR), providing predictability against foreign currency fluctuations. The platform is engineered to support diverse workloads, from single-model inference to large-scale distributed AI training, and will include 24x7 human support for mission-critical production AI workloads. ### Addressing Market Challenges [Manoj Dhanda](/tag/manoj+dhanda), Founder and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Utho Cloud, noted that the expansion aims to remove barriers limiting access to high-performance AI computing. The announcement comes amid global challenges such as GPU shortages, rising costs, and extended procurement timelines, which have impacted enterprises worldwide. Utho's platform is positioned as an alternative to conventional cloud models that often expose businesses to unpredictable GPU costs and infrastructure dependencies outside India. ## Comments ![Comment](/_icons/images/et-default-user.svg) What are your thoughts?

Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 54%, up from 52% a year earlier, driven by the data center mix shift. Infra & Chips.content: * [Home](/) * [Business Tech](/biztech) * [Business](/business) # Nebius Locks In Aug. 12 Earnings Date After Vera Rubin Rack Goes Live in Finland #### With $40B contracted and Vera Rubin online, Aug. 12 earnings will test whether NBIS’s valuation is earned By [Adrian Parham](https://www.techtimes.com/reporters/adrian-parham) [Share on Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.techtimes.com/articles/322071/20260729/nebius-locks-aug-12-earnings-date-after-vera-rubin-rack-goes-live-finland.htm) [Share on Twitter](https://x.com/intent/tweet?text=Nebius+Locks+In+Aug.+12+Earnings+Date+After+Vera+Rubin+Rack+Goes+Live+in+Finland+https://www.techtimes.com/articles/322071/20260729/nebius-locks-aug-12-earnings-date-after-vera-rubin-rack-goes-live-finland.htm) [Share on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.techtimes.com%2Farticles%2F322071%2F20260729%2Fnebius-locks-aug-12-earnings-date-after-vera-rubin-rack-goes-live-finland.htm&title=Nebius+Locks+In+Aug.+12+Earnings+Date+After+Vera+Rubin+Rack+Goes+Live+in+Finland) [Share on Reddit](http://reddit.com/submit?url=https://www.techtimes.com/articles/322071/20260729/nebius-locks-aug-12-earnings-date-after-vera-rubin-rack-goes-live-finland.htm&title=Nebius+Locks+In+Aug.+12+Earnings+Date+After+Vera+Rubin+Rack+Goes+Live+in+Finland) [Share on Flipboard](https://flipboard.com) [Share on Pocket](https://getpocket.com/edit?url=https://www.techtimes.com/articles/322071/20260729/nebius-locks-aug-12-earnings-date-after-vera-rubin-rack-goes-live-finland.htm) Nebius Group N.V. confirmed this morning that it will release second-quarter 2026 financial results on Wednesday, August 12, before U.S. market open, with a conference call at 8:00 a.m. ET per the company's [Nebius Group investor relations](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260729640472/en/Nebius-Group-announces-date-of-second-quarter-2026-results-and-conference-call) announcement. The announcement arrived six days after [Nvidia's Schedule 13G SEC filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1513845/000104581026000062/xslSCHEDULE_13G_X01/primary_doc.xml) with the Securities and Exchange Commission disclosed a 9.3% passive stake in the Amsterdam-headquartered neocloud — a filing that sent NBIS shares surging nearly 19% in a single session on July 21 and briefly pushed its market capitalization above $46 billion. Five days before that filing, Nebius had already made a different kind of financial headlines: it closed the neocloud sector's first senior secured debt facility backed by deployed GPU hardware and contracted customer cash flows — [$775 million, priced at SOFR plus 2.50%, maturing October 2030](https://nebius.com/newsroom/nebius-raises-775-million-in-first-secured-debt-financing-to-accelerate-global-buildout). And on July 23, the company announced that it had brought its [first full Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 rack online at its Mäntsälä data center in Finland](https://cryptobriefing.com/nebius-nvidia-vera-rubin-finland-ai-infrastructure/), validating the hardware that represents the frontier of commercial AI computing. Four events, ten days, and a stock still sitting 37% below its all-time high. Here is the complete decision framework. ### From Yandex's Ashes: What Nebius Actually Is Nebius's corporate biography is genuinely unusual. The company was once Yandex N.V. — the Dutch-registered parent of Russia's dominant search engine, a multi-billion-dollar conglomerate spanning search, autonomous vehicles, ride-hailing, and cloud computing founded in the late 1990s by Arkady Volozh and Ilya Segalovich. When Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022, sanctions, reputational collapse, and the freezing of Yandex's Nasdaq listing followed.
